title: Inferior Olive Neurons
intro: The inferior olive is a folded nucleus in the brainstem whose neurons send the climbing fibres to Purkinje cells. They are among the most electrically coupled neurons in the adult brain, joined by gap junctions into networks that oscillate together below threshold at a few hertz. Their rare, synchronised spikes are the cerebellum's teaching signal, and their oscillations made them a classic subject of both experiments (Llinas) and models.

items: Gap junctions: dendrites of neighbouring olivary neurons are coupled by connexin-36 gap junctions inside glomeruli, where GABAergic input from the deep cerebellar nuclei can locally shunt and so switch the coupling off (Llinas, Baker & Sotelo 1974; De Zeeuw et al. 1998).

Subthreshold oscillations: sinusoid-like membrane oscillations at about 1 to 10 Hz, produced by low-threshold (T-type) calcium current in the soma and high-threshold calcium plus calcium-activated potassium and h-currents in the dendrites (Llinas & Yarom 1981, 1986). Coupled cells oscillate in phase.

Spikes: a complex action potential: a fast sodium spike followed by a long calcium-dependent plateau with a few wavelets, then a long after-hyperpolarisation. Firing rates are very low, about 1 Hz. Each spike is relayed as a burst of a few spikes down the climbing fibre, and its exact pattern shapes the Purkinje complex spike.
Outputs: each olivary axon branches into about 7 to 10 climbing fibres in rat, each contacting one Purkinje cell; every Purkinje cell gets exactly one climbing fibre.
Inputs: excitation from the spinal cord, brainstem and the midbrain (relaying errors and unexpected events) and inhibition from the deep cerebellar nuclei, closing an olivo-cerebellar loop.

Teaching signal: in the Marr-Albus-Ito framework the climbing fibre carries an error signal, for example retinal slip during vestibulo-ocular reflex adaptation, or an unexpected air puff in eyeblink conditioning.
Timing: Llinas proposed that the oscillation is a clock that times movements; synchronised olivary firing could bind Purkinje cells into groups that control one muscle synergy (Welsh et al. 1995).

Graded signals despite all-or-none spikes: the number of spikes in the climbing fibre burst and the oscillation phase at which an input arrives change the signal, and so the plasticity, in Purkinje cells (Mathy et al. 2009; Najafi & Medina 2013).

Manor, Rinzel, Segev and Yarom (1997): showed that coupling non-oscillating, heterogeneous cells by gap junctions can create network oscillations that no single cell shows, one of the first demonstrations of emergent oscillation through electrical coupling.

Schweighofer, Doya and Kawato (1999): a two-compartment (soma and dendrite) olivary neuron model with the main calcium and potassium currents, reproducing subthreshold oscillations and complex spikes; it became the basis of later network models.

De Gruijl, Bazzigaluppi, de Jeu, De Zeeuw (2012): a three-compartment model (dendrite, soma, axon hillock) of olivary neurons fitted to in vivo and in vitro data, used in large gap-junction networks to study how coupling and inhibition shape synchrony; widely reused and ported to GPU and FPGA as a benchmark for neuromorphic hardware (e.g. Smaragdos et al. 2014).
Torben-Nielsen, Segev and Yarom (2012): network models showing how the spatial pattern of gap-junction coupling shapes travelling waves of oscillation.
Abstract: phase oscillator networks (Kuramoto-like) with tunable coupling capture the synchrony that cerebellar inhibition modulates.

blocks.text: What this means for your SNN

items: If you need a sparse, global teaching or error signal, the olive is a biological template: a small population with very low rate whose output gates plasticity in a large readout layer.

Gap junctions are easy to add to a spiking simulator (a current g_gap × (V_j − V_i) between coupled cells) and produce synchrony; add a way to switch the coupling off if you want controllable groupings.
The De Gruijl model is a good benchmark if you test a simulator or hardware on biophysically detailed, electrically coupled neurons.
